# dsm_reverse_proxy (Resource)

Manages a reverse proxy entry in Control Panel → Login Portal → Advanced → Reverse Proxy. DSM identifies entries by a UUID it assigns on creation; `description` is the only human-readable handle and must be unique.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dsm_reverse_proxy" "nextcloud" {
  description = "Nextcloud"

  source {
    protocol = "HTTPS"
    hostname = "cloud.example.com"
    port     = 443
  }

  destination {
    protocol = "HTTP"
    hostname = "localhost"
    port     = 8080
  }

  websocket = true
  http2     = true
  hsts      = true

  # Nextcloud and most single-page apps need the forwarded headers to build
  # correct absolute URLs behind the proxy.
  custom_headers = {
    "X-Forwarded-Proto" = "$scheme"
    "X-Forwarded-Host"  = "$host"
    "X-Forwarded-For"   = "$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for"
    "X-Real-IP"         = "$remote_addr"
  }

  # Optional: an access control profile that already exists in
  # Control Panel -> Login Portal -> Advanced -> Access Control Profile.
  access_control_profile = "internal-only"
}

# A minimal entry: no websocket, no custom headers, default timeouts.
resource "dsm_reverse_proxy" "metrics" {
  description = "Prometheus"

  source {
    protocol = "HTTPS"
    hostname = "metrics.example.com"
    port     = 443
  }

  destination {
    protocol = "HTTP"
    hostname = "127.0.0.1"
    port     = 9090
  }

  hsts = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Entry description shown in DSM. DSM has no separate name field, so this doubles as the entry's human-readable identity and must be unique across reverse proxy entries.

### Optional

- `access_control_profile` (String) Name of the Login Portal access control profile to apply to this entry. The profile must already exist; this provider resolves it to the UUID DSM stores.
- `custom_headers` (Map of String) Additional request headers forwarded to the destination, keyed by header name. Values may use nginx variables, for example `X-Forwarded-Proto = "$scheme"`. Header names may contain only letters, digits, and `-`. Use `websocket` rather than setting `Upgrade`/`Connection` here.
- `destination` (Block, Optional) Service requests are proxied to. Exactly one `destination` block must be declared. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--destination))
- `hsts` (Boolean) Send `Strict-Transport-Security` on the source listener. Requires an `HTTPS` source.
- `http2` (Boolean) Enable HTTP/2 on the source listener. Requires an `HTTPS` source. Not every DSM build reports this flag back; when DSM omits it the configured value is kept instead of showing drift.
- `proxy_connect_timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait when connecting to the destination.
- `proxy_intercept_errors` (Boolean) Let DSM replace destination error responses with its own error pages.
- `proxy_read_timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait for a response from the destination.
- `proxy_send_timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait while sending a request to the destination.
- `source` (Block, Optional) Public-facing listener DSM serves. Exactly one `source` block must be declared. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--source))
- `websocket` (Boolean) Add the WebSocket upgrade headers (`Upgrade: $http_upgrade` and `Connection: $connection_upgrade`). This is the same pair DSM's own WebSocket preset inserts, and it is stored alongside `custom_headers`.

### Read-Only

- `access_control_profile_id` (String) UUID of the applied access control profile, or an empty string when no profile is attached.
- `id` (String) Reverse proxy entry UUID assigned by DSM.

<a id="nestedblock--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination`

Required:

- `hostname` (String) Destination hostname or IP address, for example `localhost`. Do not include a scheme, port, or path.
- `port` (Number) Destination TCP port.
- `protocol` (String) Destination protocol: `HTTP` or `HTTPS` (for example `HTTP`). Matching is case-insensitive.


<a id="nestedblock--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Required:

- `hostname` (String) Source hostname or IP address, for example `cloud.example.com`. Do not include a scheme, port, or path.
- `port` (Number) Source TCP port.
- `protocol` (String) Source protocol: `HTTP` or `HTTPS` (for example `HTTPS`). Matching is case-insensitive.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Reverse proxy entries are identified by the UUID DSM assigns on creation.
# Find it with:
#   curl -s "$SYNOLOGY_DSM_HOST/webapi/entry.cgi?_sid=$SID" \
#     -d api=SYNO.Core.AppPortal.ReverseProxy -d version=1 -d method=list
terraform import dsm_reverse_proxy.nextcloud 1b0d0c30-9e1f-4a2b-8f7e-2c9d1a5b7e40

# The entry description is accepted too; the provider normalizes it to the UUID.
terraform import dsm_reverse_proxy.nextcloud Nextcloud
```
